claims.text: A two-stage route combining high-pressure torsion with subcritical annealing will synergistically improve strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance in high-entropy alloys.
Conventionally processed high-entropy alloys typically exhibit trade-offs among strength, ductility, stiffness, and toughness.
Conventional casting or simple thermomechanical treatment typically produces coarse or single-phase high-entropy-alloy microstructures.
High-pressure torsion will refine the grain structure.
High-pressure torsion will generate a dual-phase, multiscale architecture.
Annealing just below the order-disorder transition will nucleate coherent nanoscale precipitates.
The coherent nanoscale precipitates will form uniformly along phase boundaries.
A dual-phase microstructure with coherent boundary precipitates will promote load sharing.
The proposed microstructure will impede crack propagation.
The proposed microstructure will maintain active dislocation motion and sustained dislocation mobility.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates will reinforce phase boundaries.
Reinforcement of phase boundaries by coherent precipitates will increase lattice stiffness and Young’s modulus.
The processed alloy will achieve an approximately 10–15% increase in yield strength relative to conventionally processed alloys.
The processed alloy will achieve an approximately 10–15% increase in Young’s modulus relative to conventionally processed alloys.
The processed alloy will exhibit enhanced ductility relative to conventionally processed alloys.
The processed alloy will exhibit significantly improved crack-initiation resistance under realistic structural loading.
Annealing above the order-disorder transition may produce incoherent or brittle phases that eliminate the mechanical benefits.
Insufficient severe plastic deformation will prevent formation of a uniformly refined microstructure and undermine the expected benefits.
Very high temperatures or strain rates may override the microstructural benefits through thermal softening or dynamic failure mechanisms.
The magnitude of the improvements and precipitate coherency will depend on alloy composition and processing parameters.
